name: Discovery and business requirements
goal: Agree which decision the system will support, for whom, how success is measured and whether AI is warranted at all, before anyone designs or builds anything.
entry: A sponsor has named a problem and can give you access to the people who do the work today.

steps.title: Pick the use case and read its blueprint once, end to end
steps.output: A one-page note: what we adopt from the blueprint, and what differs here.

steps.title: Name the sponsor, the decision owner and every stakeholder
steps.output: Stakeholder map with a named decision owner.

steps.title: Answer the eight discovery questions with evidence
steps.output: Discovery log: eight questions, each with a confirmed answer, its owner and its evidence.

steps.title: Map the AS-IS process and design the TO-BE process
steps.output: AS-IS and TO-BE process maps and user journeys, agreed with the people who run them.

steps.title: Measure the baseline
steps.output: Baseline report with KPI definitions. Measured, not estimated.

steps.title: Decide whether AI is warranted at all
steps.output: AI go/no-go recommendation with the completed decision matrix.

steps.title: Classify the data and confirm the risk tier
steps.output: Data classification, confirmed risk tier and the approval path.

steps.title: Write the requirements and acceptance criteria
steps.output: Approved requirements, testable acceptance criteria and a scope boundary.

steps.title: Agree the RACI, the team and the plan
steps.output: RACI, staffing plan, dated delivery plan and risk register.

steps.title: Build the business case
steps.output: Business case with an ROI measurement plan.

steps.title: Discover the customer environment and open every access request
steps.when: Week 1, in parallel with the interviews
steps.output: Completed environment templates, a readiness report, an access and firewall request log with owners and tickets, and the agreed deployment mode.

gate.name: Gate 0 · Scope approved
checks: Every discovery question has a confirmed answer with a named owner.
The baseline is measured from real records.
The decision that AI is (or is not) warranted is recorded with its reasons.
Requirements and acceptance criteria are approved, and the out-of-scope list exists.
The risk tier and its approval path are confirmed by risk and compliance.
The RACI is agreed and every role has a named person.
The business case is approved and the next phase is funded.

traps: Starting with the model. Nothing in Phase 1 or later starts before this gate.
Accepting an estimated baseline. Without a measured one you can never show the system helped.
Treating the sponsor as the user. The person who pays is rarely the person who does the work.
A scope with no out-of-scope list.
No single named decision owner.

name: Architecture and design
goal: Turn the approved requirements into a design that fits your enterprise, meets its non-functional targets and can be built, tested, released and rolled back.

steps.title: Place the system in your enterprise landscape
steps.output: C4 context and container views and an integration matrix.

steps.title: Fix the non-functional requirements and the latency budget
steps.output: NFR matrix with a per-stage latency budget.

steps.title: Choose the model strategy and the human-oversight points
steps.output: Model strategy and oversight design, recorded as a decision record.

steps.title: Design the high-level architecture and the fallback ladder
steps.output: High-level design, sequence diagram and fallback ladder.

steps.title: Write the low-level design
steps.output: Low-level design: API contract, data model and event schema, reviewed by its consumers.

steps.title: Design the data architecture and draft the data contracts
steps.output: Data architecture and draft data contracts.

steps.title: Threat-model the design
steps.output: Threat model and security requirements.

steps.title: Size capacity and cost
steps.output: Capacity and cost model inside the business case.

steps.title: Define environments, the release path and the SLOs
steps.output: Release and environment design, and an SLO document.

steps.title: Write the test strategy
steps.output: Test strategy with a traceability matrix.

steps.title: Record the decisions and hold the architecture review
steps.output: Decision records and architecture review minutes with actions.

steps.title: Specify every integration and prove the environment can carry it
steps.output: An integration specification per hop with sequence diagrams and tests, the adapter selection, and a readiness report for the target environment.

gate.name: Gate 1 · Design approved
checks: Context, container, high-level, sequence and low-level designs are reviewed.
The stage budgets add up to the p99 latency target.
Every non-functional requirement has a target and a test that will prove it.
Every threat has a control and named evidence.
Capacity and cost fit inside the business case.
The release path, the SLOs and the rollback mechanism are defined.
Every acceptance criterion traces to a test.
Significant decisions are recorded.

traps: Copying the blueprint’s diagram without replacing its generic systems with your own.
Sizing for average load instead of peak.
No answer to “what does the user get when the model is down?”
Leaving the rollback decision to the day of the incident.
Choosing an agent because it is fashionable. Read the blueprint’s verdict first.

name: Data
goal: Get lawful access to the data, prove it is fit for purpose, and turn it into reproducible, leak-free datasets and feature pipelines.
entry: Gate 0 is signed and the data architecture from step 1.6 is drafted.

steps.title: Get access and sign the agreements
steps.output: Access approvals, signed data contracts, the privacy impact assessment and a customer-environment checklist with every blocker owned.

steps.title: Profile the data
steps.output: Data profiling report and a quality issues log.

steps.title: Write the source-to-target mapping
steps.output: Source-to-target mapping that reconciles to a trusted report.

steps.title: Define the label and the prediction point
steps.output: Label specification approved by the domain expert.

steps.title: Build the ingestion pipelines
steps.output: Ingestion pipelines running in development, with lineage.

steps.title: Add automated data-quality gates
steps.output: Automated quality checks that block bad data, and a dashboard.

steps.title: Build the features, correct as of the prediction time
steps.output: Feature pipelines and feature definitions, with a test that proves no feature uses future data.

steps.title: Create the training, validation and test datasets
steps.output: Versioned datasets with a dataset card, reproducible from code.

steps.title: Explore the data and confirm the signal
steps.output: Exploration report with signal and leakage findings.

gate.name: Gate 2 · Data ready
checks: Access is approved for this purpose and the data contracts are signed.
Quality checks are automated and passing.
The label definition is approved by the domain expert.
A test proves no feature uses information from after the prediction time.
Datasets are versioned and can be rebuilt from code.
The signal is confirmed against the baseline, or the work has gone back to Gate 0.

traps: A random train/test split on time-dependent data.
A feature filled in after the outcome is known.
A one-off notebook extraction nobody can re-run.
Defining the label without the domain expert.
Different feature code for training and for serving.

name: Model and application build
goal: Build a baseline, beat it with a candidate, and turn the result into packaged, reproducible, callable software inside the user’s workflow.
entry: Gate 1 is signed. Model training starts when Gate 2 is signed; repository and serving work can start earlier.

steps.title: Set up the repository, CI and experiment tracking
steps.output: Repository, CI, experiment tracking and model registry.

steps.title: Run the starter kit and build the baseline
steps.output: Baseline with an evaluation report: the number every later model must beat.

steps.title: Build the candidate model
steps.output: Candidate model, experiment log and error analysis.

steps.title: Evaluate, calibrate and set the operating point
steps.output: Evaluation report and an operating point signed by the decision owner.

steps.title: Package the model and build the training pipeline
steps.output: Reproducible training pipeline and a registered model.

steps.title: Build the serving path
steps.output: Inference service running in development, with its fallbacks.

steps.title: Optimise inference
steps.output: Performance report: the latency budget is met at the planned cost.

steps.title: Build the application and the human-in-the-loop
steps.output: Application integrated into the workflow, with feedback capture.

steps.title: Build the evaluation harness and the guardrails
steps.output: Evaluation harness in CI and guardrails in the request path.

steps.title: Write the model card
steps.output: Model card and, where required, the governance submission.

gate.name: Gate 3 · Build complete
checks: The candidate beats the baseline on the untouched test set by the agreed margin, or the baseline is what ships.
The operating point is approved by the decision owner.
The training pipeline reproduces the metrics from a clean checkout.
Serving meets the latency budget in development.
The fallback ladder is implemented and tested.
The evaluation harness runs in CI.
The model card is complete.

traps: Skipping the baseline, so nobody knows what the complex model added.
Tuning on the test set.
A model that only runs in a notebook.
A threshold chosen by the data scientist alone.
Reporting only the average metric and never the slices.
No fallback path.

name: Platform, security and verification
goal: Prove, in an environment that resembles production, that the system meets its requirements, is secure, can be observed, and can be rolled back.
entry: Gate 1 is signed for platform work. Testing of a component starts as soon as it exists; the full run needs Gate 3.

steps.title: Provision the environments as code
steps.output: Staging and production environments created from code.

steps.title: Build the deployment pipeline
steps.output: Deployment pipeline with promotion gates and rollback.

steps.title: Instrument observability
steps.output: Dashboards, alerts and a prediction log.

steps.title: Run functional, contract and integration tests
steps.output: Test report and automated suites.

steps.title: Load-test and inject faults
steps.output: Performance and resilience report.

steps.title: Test security and give sign-off
steps.output: Security test report and sign-off.

steps.title: Review responsible AI and compliance
steps.output: Compliance evidence pack and approvals.

steps.title: Run user acceptance testing
steps.output: Acceptance test report signed by the product owner.

steps.title: Write the runbooks and train support
steps.output: Runbooks, on-call rota and trained support.

steps.title: Rehearse rollback and disaster recovery
steps.output: Rollback and recovery rehearsal record, with timings.

steps.title: Run customer acceptance testing and plan adoption
steps.output: Signed customer acceptance, a defect and exception log, training records and an adoption plan.

gate.name: Gate 4 · Ready for release
checks: Every acceptance criterion passes.
No critical or high defect or vulnerability is open.
The load test meets the non-functional targets at peak.
Every failure scenario has an alert and a runbook, and has been exercised.
Rollback has been rehearsed and timed.
User acceptance is signed.
The compliance approvals are in hand.

traps: A staging environment that does not resemble production.
Testing only the happy path.
Alerts with no owner.
“We will write the runbooks after go-live.”
A rollback nobody has ever run.

name: Release and deployment
goal: Put the system in front of real traffic gradually, prove the business effect with a planned experiment, and hand a working service to operations.

steps.title: Prepare the business change
steps.output: Users trained, communication sent, procedures updated.

steps.title: Plan the cut-over and the experiment
steps.output: Rollout and experiment plan, written before any traffic moves.

steps.title: Hold the go/no-go review
steps.output: Recorded go/no-go decision and an approved change request.

steps.title: Deploy to production with no user impact
steps.output: Production deployment verified, with users still on the old path.

steps.title: Run in shadow
steps.output: Shadow report: production behaves as offline evaluation predicted.

steps.title: Canary, then ramp
steps.output: Ramp log with the decision taken at each step.

steps.title: Measure the business effect
steps.output: Experiment readout.

steps.title: Run hypercare and hand over to operations
steps.output: Production handover package and a signed acceptance record: the service is accepted by operations.

steps.title: Close the release
steps.output: Release record and retrospective actions.

gate.name: Gate 5 · Live and accepted
checks: The planned share of traffic has been served inside the SLO for the agreed period.
No guardrail metric was breached.
The experiment readout is delivered.
Rollback stayed available throughout the ramp.
Operations has accepted the handover.
The release evidence is archived.

traps: A big-bang release to everyone at once.
Declaring success before the labels have matured.
Changing the success metric after seeing the data.
Nobody owns the rollback decision.
Skipping user training.

name: Operate, monitor and improve
goal: Keep the service reliable, the model accurate, the cost under control and the benefit visible, for as long as the system runs.
entry: Gate 5 is signed. This phase does not end: it repeats until the system is retired.

steps.title: Watch service health
steps.output: SLO report.

steps.title: Monitor data quality and drift
steps.output: Drift and data-quality dashboard with alerts.

steps.title: Monitor model performance
steps.output: Weekly model performance review.

steps.title: Track business value and adoption
steps.when: Monthly, with a quarterly value review
steps.output: Benefit report against the baseline.

steps.title: Control the cost
steps.output: Cost report and optimisation actions.

steps.title: Handle incidents and learn from them
steps.output: Incident record and review actions.

steps.title: Retrain, challenge and roll back
steps.when: On a trigger: drift, a performance drop, a schedule or a data change
steps.output: Retraining record: a new champion, or a documented rejection.

steps.title: Keep security and compliance current
steps.when: Continuous scanning, quarterly access review, periodic model review
steps.output: Compliance evidence log.

steps.title: Collect feedback and manage the backlog
steps.output: Prioritised backlog.

steps.title: Review the service: continue, change or retire
steps.output: Quarterly service review decision.

steps.title: Coordinate customer-side incidents and change windows
steps.output: An incident and change log for customer-side events, current environment documentation and a monthly report to the product owner.

gate.name: Gate 6 · Quarterly service review
checks: The SLOs were met, or the error-budget policy was applied.
Model performance is inside the agreed band, or a retrain has been done.
The realised benefit is reported against the baseline.
Incidents are reviewed and their actions closed.
Cost is inside the budget.
The compliance evidence is current.

traps: Monitoring uptime only. A model can be up, fast and wrong.
No way for the true outcomes to flow back, so performance is never measured.
Automatic retraining with no evaluation gate.
So many alerts that people stop reading them.
Nobody owns the model once the project team has moved on.
